display.purpose: Room titles at the head of each view; Bricolage Grotesque, condensed (wdth 84) and tightly tracked.

headline.purpose: The chapter h1 on the ivory reading table.

title.purpose: Section h2, drawer titles, bay/card/slip headings; often engraved with a two-way text-shadow on wood.

body.purpose: Reading passages in Literata, held to a 66ch measure with opsz 16.

label.purpose: Uppercase, wide-tracked Azeret Mono for every datum, meta row, and engraved section marker.

shadows.name: seated-furniture
shadows.purpose: Drawer stacks and the vitrine: deep pooled shadow paired with a lit top edge.

shadows.name: table-lifted
shadows.purpose: The ivory reading table, lifted highest, with a warm 3px front edge.

shadows.name: drawer-hover
shadows.purpose: Sideways shadow as a drawer slides out on hover/focus.

shadows.name: drawer-ajar
shadows.purpose: A half-open drawer: deeper side shadow plus the baize edge-light that appears only when open.

shadows.name: paper-lifted
shadows.purpose: Catalogue cards and cross-reference slips at rest; deepens to 0 20px 30px -18px on hover.

shadows.name: slip-overlay
shadows.purpose: The right-hand catalogue slip drawer over its blurred veil.

shadows.name: float-loupe
shadows.purpose: The floating selection loupe; the toast uses the similar 0 20px 34px -20px.

motion.name: e-out
motion.purpose: Default easing for hovers, fades, rises, and state transitions.

motion.name: e-drawer
motion.purpose: The furniture gesture: drawer glide and the catalogue slip's slide-in.

motion.name: rise
motion.value: keyframes: from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(7px); } — 0.38s e-out
motion.purpose: The one authored gesture on the ivory table: a text block rises as extent reveals it.

motion.name: slipIn
motion.purpose: The catalogue slip enters from the right edge.

motion.name: fade
motion.purpose: The slip veil fades up behind the panel.

motion.name: reduced-motion-reset
motion.purpose: Full motion reset: every animation and transition is neutralized.

breakpoints.name: wall-2col
breakpoints.purpose: Cabinet wall drops from 3 to 2 columns.

breakpoints.name: table-stack
breakpoints.purpose: Reading table collapses to one column; label card un-sticks; extent dial reflows 2-up.

breakpoints.name: compact
breakpoints.purpose: Rail wraps and tool labels hide; vitrine and wall go 1 column; slip full-width; rail height 54px.

components.name: Drawer
components.description: A flush walnut drawer in the cabinet wall; clicking routes to its chapter on the reading table. Newest drawers stand half-open on their baize.
components.css: .ds-stack { border: 1px solid #4a3a29; border-radius: 3px; background: #0f0b07; overflow: hidden; box-shadow: 0 30px 54px -34px rgba(0,0,0,1), 0 1px 0 rgba(255,228,180,.07) inset; } .ds-drawer { position: relative; display: block; width: 100%; text-align: left; appearance: none; cursor: pointer; border: 0; padding: 0; background: linear-gradient(180deg, #33281d 0%, #292017 62%, #241b13 100%); color: #ece0cb; transition: transform .42s cubic-bezier(.2,.9,.25,1), box-shadow .42s cubic-bezier(.2,.9,.25,1), filter .3s cubic-bezier(.16,.84,.3,1); } .ds-drawer-ajar { transform: translateX(12px); box-shadow: -18px 0 26px -16px rgba(0,0,0,.95), inset 1px 0 0 #3f6853, inset 9px 0 16px -9px rgba(0,0,0,.9); } .ds-drawer:hover { transform: translateX(6px); filter: brightness(1.1); box-shadow: -14px 0 22px -14px rgba(0,0,0,.95); } .ds-drawer-in { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 44px 1fr auto; align-items: center; gap: .85rem; padding: 1.15rem 1.2rem; } .ds-spec { width: 40px; height: 40px; opacity: .92; } .ds-drawer-title { display: block; margin: 0 0 .22rem; font: 600 1.06rem/1.22 "Bricolage Grotesque", sans-serif; font-variation-settings: "wdth" 92; letter-spacing: -.012em; color: #f0e4cf; text-shadow: 0 1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,.6), 0 -1px 0 rgba(255,232,190,.07); } .ds-drawer-meta { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: .5rem; font: 400 .64rem/1.5 "Azeret Mono", monospace; letter-spacing: .1em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #a5947d; } .ds-acc { color: #bd9445; } .ds-state { padding: .1rem .38rem; border-radius: 2px; letter-spacing: .12em; border: 1px solid currentColor; } .ds-st-new { color: #7fc9a4; } .ds-pull { width: 30px; height: 9px; border-radius: 2px; background: linear-gradient(180deg, #edc264, #c9962f 42%, #8a6a2a); box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.7), 0 1px 0 rgba(255,240,205,.45) inset; } .ds-drawer-read { position: absolute; left: 0; bottom: 0; width: 100%; height: 2px; background: #c9962f; transform-origin: left; transform: scaleX(.4); }

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The committing action on the ivory table: keep a card, file a round, advance. Solid brass with ink text.
components.css: .ds-btn-brass { appearance: none; cursor: pointer; padding: .48rem .85rem; border-radius: 3px; border: 1px solid #7d5f22; background: linear-gradient(180deg, #edc264, #c9962f 55%, #8a6a2a); color: #1e1608; font: 500 .8rem/1 "Bricolage Grotesque", sans-serif; letter-spacing: .01em; box-shadow: 0 1px 0 rgba(255,246,220,.6) inset; transition: background .18s cubic-bezier(.16,.84,.3,1), transform .15s cubic-bezier(.16,.84,.3,1); } .ds-btn-brass:hover { background: linear-gradient(180deg, #f6d894, #edc264 55%, #c9962f); } .ds-btn-brass:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn-brass:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #edc264; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: The table-surface default action: warm ivory gradient with ink text.
components.css: .ds-btn { appearance: none; cursor: pointer; padding: .48rem .85rem; border-radius: 3px; border: 1px solid rgba(120,96,50,.4); background: linear-gradient(180deg, #fdfaf4, #eee3d1); color: #241d14; font: 500 .8rem/1 "Bricolage Grotesque", sans-serif; transition: background .18s cubic-bezier(.16,.84,.3,1), transform .15s cubic-bezier(.16,.84,.3,1), border-color .18s cubic-bezier(.16,.84,.3,1); } .ds-btn:hover { background: linear-gradient(180deg, #fffdf8, #e6d9c2); border-color: rgba(120,96,50,.7); } .ds-btn:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #edc264; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Filter Chip
components.description: Area filter on the cabinet wall. Solo-first: a plain click focuses one area, clicking the focused one clears back to all, shift-click combines. A leading "All areas" chip is pressed whenever nothing is soloed, and a hint line spells both gestures out.
components.html: Click to focus one · shift-click to combine
components.css: .ds-chip { appearance: none; cursor: pointer; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: .4rem; padding: .34rem .62rem; background: rgba(255,240,214,.045); border: 1px solid rgba(201,150,47,.22); border-radius: 999px; color: #b3a08a; font: 500 .71rem/1 "Bricolage Grotesque", sans-serif; letter-spacing: .02em; transition: background .2s, color .2s, border-color .2s; } .ds-chip .ds-dot { width: .5rem; height: .5rem; border-radius: 50%; background: currentColor; } .ds-chip:hover { background: rgba(255,240,214,.1); color: #ece0cb; } .ds-chip[aria-pressed="true"] { color: #ece0cb; border-color: currentColor; background: rgba(255,240,214,.11); } .ds-chip:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #edc264; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-chiprow { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: .4rem; } .ds-chip-all { letter-spacing: .04em; text-transform: none; } .ds-hint { color: #8d7d68; font: 400 .68rem/1.3 "Bricolage Grotesque", sans-serif; margin-left: .3rem; }

components.name: Catalogue Card
components.description: Catalogue entry for one concept or fundamental pattern. Cards live in an auto-fill grid with dense flow so the heaviest concepts can span two columns without leaving holes; the weight footer is pinned to the bottom so every card in a row bottoms out on the same line.
components.css: .ds-card { appearance: none; cursor: pointer; text-align: left; position: relative; padding: .7rem .85rem .75rem; background: linear-gradient(178deg, color-mix(in srgb, var(--t) 7%, #fbf6ec), color-mix(in srgb, var(--t) 4%, #ebdfcc)); border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--t) 24%, #c9b99d); border-radius: 2px; color: #241d14; max-width: 27ch; box-shadow: 0 10px 20px -16px rgba(0,0,0,.95); transition: transform .22s cubic-bezier(.16,.84,.3,1), box-shadow .22s cubic-bezier(.16,.84,.3,1); } .ds-card:hover { transform: translateY(-3px) rotate(-.35deg); box-shadow: 0 20px 30px -18px rgba(0,0,0,.95); } .ds-card-kind { font: 500 .58rem/1 "Azeret Mono", monospace; letter-spacing: .16em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--t); } .ds-card-term { display: block; margin: .28rem 0 .3rem; font: 600 1rem/1.2 "Bricolage Grotesque", sans-serif; font-variation-settings: "wdth" 92; letter-spacing: -.015em; color: #241d14; } .ds-card-short { display: block; font: 400 .8rem/1.42 "Literata", Georgia, serif; color: #5f5445; } .ds-card-mag { display: block; margin-top: .45rem; font: 400 .6rem/1 "Azeret Mono", monospace; letter-spacing: .1em; color: #6f6555; } .ds-card:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #edc264; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Rail Tool
components.description: A brass control in the head rail (Random, Room light); pressed state fills solid brass. On narrow screens the label collapses to the icon.
components.css: .ds-tool { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: .42rem; appearance: none; cursor: pointer; padding: .44rem .72rem; background: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(201,150,47,.16), rgba(201,150,47,.06)); border: 1px solid rgba(201,150,47,.34); border-radius: 3px; color: #edc264; font: 500 .76rem/1 "Bricolage Grotesque", sans-serif; letter-spacing: .02em; transition: background .2s, border-color .2s, transform .2s; } .ds-tool .ds-ic { width: 1.05em; height: 1.05em; fill: none; stroke: currentColor; stroke-width: 1.6; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round; } .ds-tool:hover { background: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(201,150,47,.3), rgba(201,150,47,.13)); border-color: rgba(237,194,100,.6); } .ds-tool:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-tool[aria-pressed="true"] { background: linear-gradient(180deg, #c9962f, #8a6a2a); color: #1e1608; border-color: #edc264; } .ds-tool:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #edc264; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Inline Concept Term
components.description: A concept reference woven into reading prose; its computed importance (tier 1–4) is encoded in the underline weight and, at the top tier, small caps.
components.html: Wait time explodes as a queue approaches , which makes precise.
components.css: .ds-read-p { font: 400 1.14rem/1.63 "Literata", Georgia, serif; font-variation-settings: "opsz" 16; color: #2b2317; max-width: 66ch; } .ds-term { appearance: none; background: none; border: 0; padding: 0; cursor: pointer; font: inherit; color: var(--t, #241d14); text-decoration: underline; text-underline-offset: .17em; text-decoration-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--t, #241d14) 42%, transparent); border-radius: 2px; transition: background .16s, text-decoration-color .16s; } .ds-w2 { text-decoration-thickness: 1px; } .ds-w4 { text-decoration-thickness: 2.5px; font-weight: 600; font-variant-caps: all-small-caps; letter-spacing: .045em; } .ds-term:hover { background: rgba(201,150,47,.2); text-decoration-color: var(--t, #241d14); }

components.name: Wall Legend
components.description: An open-by-default disclosure above the drawer wall that decodes every encoding on it. Each entry pairs a literal swatch with the sentence that names what it means. Dismissible, persisted, never hidden on first contact.
components.html:
What the drawers are telling you
Drawer depth is reading length — deeper drawer, longer chapter.A green baize seam down the left means the drawer stands ajar: new, or revised since you last looked.The brass line along the bottom is how far through it you already are.A struck-through title is retiring — superseded, kept only until you have read its replacement.
components.css: .ds-key { border-top: 1px solid rgba(255,240,214,.07); padding-top: .7rem; } .ds-key summary { cursor: pointer; list-style: none; color: #b3a08a; font: 500 .68rem/1 "Bricolage Grotesque", sans-serif; letter-spacing: .12em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-key summary::before { content: "\25c7"; margin-right: .45rem; color: #c9962f; } .ds-keygrid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(15rem, 1fr)); gap: .5rem 1.2rem; margin-top: .7rem; } .ds-keyrow { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1.6rem 1fr; align-items: start; color: #b3a08a; font: 400 .78rem/1.45 "Literata", Georgia, serif; } .ds-k { margin-top: .35rem; } .ds-k-depth { width: 1.1rem; height: .62rem; background: linear-gradient(180deg,#3a2a18,#2a1d10); border-radius: 2px; } .ds-k-baize { width: 3px; height: .9rem; background: #2e8f74; border-radius: 1px; } .ds-k-read { width: 1.1rem; height: 2px; background: #c9962f; margin-top: .6rem; } .ds-k-strike { width: 1.1rem; height: 1px; background: #b9564c; margin-top: .6rem; }

components.name: Provenance List
components.description: The numbered source list closing every chapter, set on the ivory table. An entry becomes a brass link when it has a URL and stays plain text when it does not — a citation without a link is a first-class citation, never a fabricated one.
components.html:
Where this came from

  1. OneLake shortcuts — Microsoft LearnLimits: 100,000 per item, 10 per path, 5 chained links.learn.microsoft.com
  2. Little, J. D. C. (2011). Little's Law as viewed on its 50th anniversary.
components.css: .ds-prov { border-top: 1px solid rgba(60,42,20,.16); padding-top: .9rem; color: #3c2f1e; } .ds-prov h3 { font: 500 .68rem/1 "Bricolage Grotesque", sans-serif; letter-spacing: .14em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #7a6549; margin: 0 0 .7rem; } .ds-provlist { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; counter-reset: p; } .ds-provlist li { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1.9rem 1fr; margin-bottom: .55rem; counter-increment: p; } .ds-provlist li::before { content: counter(p); grid-column: 1; grid-row: 1; font: 400 .74rem/1.5 "Azeret Mono", monospace; color: #a08a63; } .ds-provlist li > * { grid-column: 2; } .ds-provlist a { color: #8a6b1f; text-decoration: underline; text-underline-offset: 2px; font: 400 .88rem/1.5 "Literata", Georgia, serif; } .ds-provcite { font: 400 .88rem/1.5 "Literata", Georgia, serif; } .ds-provnote { display: block; font: 400 .8rem/1.45 "Literata", Georgia, serif; color: #6a5842; } .ds-provhost { display: block; font: 400 .68rem/1.4 "Azeret Mono", monospace; color: #a08a63; }

narrative.overview:
Knowledge Cabinet is a private collection housed in a piece of furniture, not a reading app. The room and its cabinet are dark walnut; drawers of unequal depth sit flush in a wall, each fitted with a brass hairline pull. Pulling a drawer brings its chapter to rest on the single warm ivory reading table — the only light surface in the entire room. Baize-green linings only flash into view along the edge of a drawer that stands half-open. The pleasure is spatial and tactile: you find queueing theory filed beside memory research because they happen to share a wall, and you refuse the left-rail-contents-beside-a-cream-column arrangement of every other reading tool.

The mood is museum-quiet, warm, and slightly analog — lamplight, brass, wood grain, and dotted rule lines instead of chrome and cards. Density is deliberate but never cramped: the vitrine and cabinet breathe at wide measure (up to 1320px), while reading prose is held to a strict 66ch. Motion is furniture motion — a drawer glides, a text block rises, a catalogue slip slides in from the right — one authored gesture per surface, nothing decorative. The system commits hard to two textures and refuses a third: there is exactly one light surface (the table), and everything else lives on walnut.

The five growth areas — Technical (primary), Communication, Learning, Memory, Thinking — each get an authored specimen plate (a hand-drawn SVG “insect” pinned in the drawer) and a two-tone area ink. Importance is not decoration here: a concept’s weight is computed at load and made visible four different ways, because the system asserts there is no single correct way to make importance legible.
keyCharacteristics: Two surfaces only: dark walnut room/cabinet, one ivory reading table.
Nearly square corners (2–4px) with brass hairline (1px) fittings.
Three type roles: Bricolage Grotesque (display/UI), Literata (reading), Azeret Mono (data/labels).
Five area inks, each in a graphic and a text-on-ivory variant.
One authored gesture per surface; a full prefers-reduced-motion reset.
Importance is a real, computed, four-way-encoded mechanism.

rules.name: The Two-Surface Rule
rules.body: There are exactly two material surfaces. The room, rail, cabinet wall, drawers, vitrine, catalogue controls, rounds thread, register, slip, loupe, and toast all live on walnut and use the on-cab text ramp. The reading table, label card, extent dial, figures, catalogue cards, round cards, and slip cards live on ivory and use the ink ramp. A component picks one surface and never mixes the two ramps.

rules.name: The One-Metal Rule
rules.body: Brass is the only metallic accent and it means “actionable / current.” Never introduce a second metal or spend brass on inert decoration; its scarcity is what makes a pull read as a pull.

rules.name: The Read-Brass Rule
rules.body: Brass that must be read uses brass-label (or brass-lit on dark); brass-dim is gradient-shadow only and never carries text.

rules.name: The 66ch Rule
rules.body: Reading prose (h1/h2/p/ul/aside/pre/prompt on the table) is capped at max-width: 66ch; specimens and figures are allowed the full table width (min(100%, 62rem)). The measure is achieved per-element inside a wide table, not by narrowing the whole surface.

rules.name: The Three-Role Rule
rules.body: Sans for display and UI, serif for reading, mono for data and labels. Never set a passage in the grotesque or a label in the serif; the typeface is the signal of what kind of text this is.

rules.name: The Engraved-Label Rule
rules.body: Uppercase mono micro-labels always carry wide tracking (0.1em on meta, 0.13–0.2em on .eng/section markers). Tracked, uppercased mono reads as an engraved plate; tight or lowercase mono reads as a value.

rules.name: The Lit-Edge Rule
rules.body: Every seated surface (drawer, vitrine, table, round card) pairs its pooled drop shadow with a 1px inset top highlight. Shadow alone reads as a flat cutout; the lit edge is what makes it wood or glass.

rules.name: The Baize-Only-When-Open Rule
rules.body: The baize-green lining (baize-lit) is depth information, not color: it appears solely as an inset edge on a half-open drawer. Never paint baize on a closed or flat surface.

rules.name: The Hard-Corner Rule
rules.body: Nothing in the interior exceeds a 4px radius except the two pill exceptions (chips, count badge). If a new surface wants a soft, rounded-card look, it is wrong for this world — go to 2–3px.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Structural separation is a 1px hairline, never a heavy divider or a filled bar. On walnut it is translucent brass; on ivory it is ivory-3, dotted when it separates rows of the same object.

rules: Every encoding on a surface is named once, in place. The wall legend and the catalogue notes are not help text — they are part of the composition, and they open by default.
A filter is solo-first: one click focuses, one click releases. "All selected" and "none selected" normalise to the same state so the view never has two identical-looking truths.
A citation without a URL renders as plain text. Never invent a link to make a row look uniform.
dos: Do keep every component on exactly one surface: walnut with the on-cab ramp, or ivory with the ink ramp (The Two-Surface Rule).
Do spend brass only on actionable or current elements, and pull readable brass from brass-label/brass-lit, never brass-dim.
Do hold reading prose to 66ch while letting specimens and figures use the full table width.
Do keep corners hard — 2px inner, 3px panels/controls, 4px only for the table/round cards/loupe; pills only for chips and the count badge.
Do separate with 1px hairlines (translucent brass on walnut, ivory-3 — dotted for same-object rows — on ivory) and pair every seated surface with a 1px inset lit edge.
Do keep type in its role: Bricolage for display/UI, Literata for reading, Azeret Mono (tracked, uppercased) for labels and data.
Do give motion one authored gesture per surface (drawer glides, block rises, slip slides) and honor the full prefers-reduced-motion reset.
Do encode concept importance with the real --mag / --warm mechanism (size / lamplight / engraving / threads), not ad-hoc emphasis.
donts: Don’t introduce a second light surface or a second metal — the ivory table and brass are each singular.
Don’t show baize green anywhere except as the inset edge of a half-open drawer.
Don’t use rounded-card radii (≥6px), drop shadows without a lit edge, or heavy/filled dividers.
Don’t set a passage in the grotesque or a label in the serif; don’t leave uppercase mono labels untracked.
Don’t put a left-rail contents list beside a cream essay column — that reading-app arrangement is the explicit anti-reference.

Don’t hard-code area-ink hex in new code paths; the --a-* tokens are the source of truth. Known duplication: app.js carries an INK map restating the --a-* graphic and -t text values, and content.js areas[].ink holds a third, slightly different set used only in the content model — reconcile to the CSS tokens rather than adding a fourth.
